posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
The problem with making an "algorithim" is that there are so many little interactions that give rise to so many edge cases it would be extremely hard to get a solid one down. You want a one size fits all theory of how to resolve effects, which kind of betrays the complexity of all the different interactions.

The best way to look at it is in the sense of Triggers and Effects:

For consecutive triggers and overlapping effects, the newest triggered effects take precedance over older ones. 

During simultanious triggered effects (multiple end of turn boss effects for example), you start with the oldest and move to the newest. 

That is all you need.

As for damage taken/delt, there is no distinction within the game. Delt/taken are the same for all intents and purposes, as damage delt is always the result of HP loss.

So far phataskippy came closest to what I was looking for in his list.  It does imply some things I hadn't thought through; eg, I'm not sure if there are any redirect effects that depend on the damage size, but if there were, it would have to depend on the damage _before_ any target-specific effects.  I gather from some of the other answers that damage type modifications are a separate step (between your steps 1 and 2).  I would also add a separate step for target selection, which it seems is its own thing, from the earlier settled answers about when you can select different targets and the like.  That's part of step 1 in your list, I guess.

Mr. Fixer can redirect damage of 2 or less, if his damage reduction would lower damage dealt to 2 or 1 he redirects it, no matter what its original amount was.  As I recently learned the damage then returns to its full amount (since MR. Fixers pipe wrench isn't protecting anyone else), which is why redirection sends you back to recalculate on my list.

Damage type gets modified just like damage, there can be any number of modifiers out there, they each get their own little process, but I put them in two categories, modifiers to the damage source's damage dealt, and modifiers to the target's damage taken.  I do it this way because the damage source never changes.  Do all the various calculations to the source in step two, and the current target in step 4.  Modify the damge fully before redirection anytime the redirection is triggered by damage dealt to a target. (Like with Mr. Fixer)

I don't include a targetting step, that is part of step one, adn the reason is some damage doesn't require you to select a target.

As for infinite loop, that would require an infinite loop of redirection, which does not occur.

The list would make more sense with damage type being determined as a step by itself, I do it together, since most cards that change type also modify it.  If you would prefer it seperate, just add it in and make the list 10 steps.

The order of damage reduction is a difficult thing.  I would expect one of two routes:

1.  The effects go off in the order the cards entered play (this is a rule for card effects that go off end of turn and such, it may apply the same)  I don't follow that as I don't like to keep track of that, and players aren't the best at putting their cards in play in an orderly cronological fashion.

2.  The effects would trigger simultaneously (Like damaging all targets at once, you have multiple cards trying to reduce the damage at once) and therefore the heroes choose the order.  I prefer this method myself.  It is more fun, adds to the "Thinking and then being triumphant" aspect of the game, and it benefits me and my friends.  Also who really wants to sit there and try to line up damage reduction cards coming into play for maximum benefit?

In the end the creators of this game seem to me to value fun over regulation, so don't stress too much over the little rules, if your players find one way better, use it.

phantaskippy:

In the end the creators of this game seem to me to value fun over regulation, so don't stress too much over the little rules, if your players find one way better, use it.

This may be the most relevant text!

 

FWIW, here's my algorithm:

Given the source of an attack, the destination of an attack (target), the type  of an attack, and the amount of an attack:
 
  1. Apply all cards that affect the type of the attack in card played order. (This is only done as an separate, first step, because there are no cards which change the type of an attack based on either the destination of the attack or the amount of the attack, and there are no cards which change the source of an attack).
  2. Apply all other cards in card played order. If a card changes the destinatio n of the attack (target), reset the amount of the attack to the original amount  and return to the beginning of this step, but don't consider that card again. 
  3. If the attack is 0 or less or the target is immune, no damage is dealt.
 
Other relevant rules and effects:
  • An attack that has been reduced to zero or less can NOT be  redirected.
  • Stored increase (Haka of Battle) or reduction (Wraith's Stealth)  are applied in card played order as well.
  • There is no established order of the hero and villain character cards, so I would let that be a player decision, if it ever came up. Another thought would be to say the order is the order of turns, so villain character cards first followed by each hero character card.
 

Basically, card played order is King. Some perhaps non-intuitive results can occur. For instance, if Mr. Fixer is hitting himself due to an Infection and has a plus one from a tool and a plus one from Harmony, whether or not he can redirect due to Praying Mantis is going to depend on the order in which his cards were played. Praying Mantis before one or both of the tool and Harmony? Amount is one or two, so redirection! After both? Amount is three, so not redirected.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
It is not a constant effect, there are effects that cover a period of time, like immunity and indestructibility.  You are right that Imbued fire changes the damage type to fire.

This does not allow for boosting a single instance of damage as both projectile and fire.  Because it cannot be both projectile and fire.

Damage reduction does not carry in redirection, because it only protects the target that has it, if damage going to Tachyon is reduced, then redirected to a target that isn't covered by the reduction Tachyon has, then the damage is not reduced by that reduction.  Same with Micro Targetting computer and imbued fire, whenever the damage type is changed conditional modifiers have to be reevaluated, in case the condition of the modification is no longer applicable.

As a point that is a bit away from the discussion, and to repeat my earlier stance:  I believe that optional modifiers like TTE can be applied at will within the time frame of their activation.  If TTE is played, then Imbued fire, then close quarters combat, when the hero with TTE sitting next to their card would deal damage it is changed to fire and then melee, throughout that process it is still in the "would be dealt damage" phase, and I would say that Visionary could choose to wait until both had triggered and resolved before activating the effect of TTE, still in proper timing, since it is still the "would be dealt damage" timing.

The best sense of an order we have is the text "would deal damage" vs. "Deals damage", (or be dealt if it's defensive)  I posted what I think is a pretty good resolution order, I seperated the damage type and amount modifers, simply because it makes it easier to keep straight. I'll repost it here:

1:  Damage Declaration, initial Source, type, amount and target are declared.

2:  Apply changes to damage type.

3:  Apply modifiers to damage based on source and type.

4:  Source of damage steps complete, check for redirection based on source, proceed to target.

5.  If target is immune end damage calculations, no damage is dealt.

6.  Trigger all "would be dealt damage" reduction and redirection effects.

7.  Trigger all "is dealt damage" modifiers.

8,  Reduce targets HP.

Step 5 exists because of an official ruling that you can't redirect damage that the hero is immune to, since they could not be dealt that damage.  Officially inside each step you should go by card order, although on steps 6 and 7 I tend to let the heroes choose the order, because it gets annoying to keep track of which cards were played first, and arguments don't improve the game when someone misremembers.
